title: ALMA 0.88 mm Survey of Disks around Planetary-mass Companions
question: Do disks around planetary-mass companions follow the disk flux-host mass trend of stellar disks, or are they fainter (e.g., like binary-star disks)?

what.value: Literature disk fluxes of stars/brown dwarfs in Taurus, Cha I, Lupus, Upper Sco for flux-mass relation

evidence.quote: Disk fluxes of stars and brown dwarfs are compiled from millimeter studies of star-forming regions, including Taurus

external_data.citation: (cite: A13; Ricci14; WD18; Pascucci16; Long18; Ansdell16; Sanchis20; Barenfeld16; V16)

what.value: Upper limits for GSC 6214-210 b, GQ Lup b, 2M1207 b and PDS 70 b,c fluxes

evidence.quote: $<$200 $\mu$Jy for GSC 6214-210 b, (cite: Bowler15); $<$150 $\mu$Jy for GQ Lup b, (cite: M17); $<$78 $\mu$Jy for 2M1207 b, (cite: R17)

recipe.method: Archive calibration scripts; self-calibration for CT Cha and DH Tau
key_parameters: phase solint 400 s to 30 s; amplitude 30 s

recipe.method: tclean natural-weighted MFS; aperture photometry of beam area for undetected sources; elliptical gaussian visibility fit for detected hosts

recipe.goal: Fit disk flux vs host mass relation
recipe.method: Bayesian linear regression with linmix including non-detections, fluxes scaled to 140 pc, extrapolated to planetary masses
assumptions: Fluxes not converted to dust masses because of optical depth uncertainty
